h1.no_claim_reason: the title says 'MEIS1 transcriptional dysregulation ... causes' RLS and the mechanism says MEIS1 variants 'may disrupt transcriptional programs': dysregulation is undirected (guide: 'dysregulates X' has no sign), so no direction for MEIS1 is stated. The only signed statement is about the variant rs113851554-T (beta 0.669, and the falsification's 'increase RLS risk'), which the chain never names; the chain starts at MEIS1.

h2.note: sign read from the title 'BTBD9 synaptic dysfunction leads to ...' as loss-of-function wording (impaired BTBD9 causes the disease), consistent with the falsification, which tests BTBD9 knockout mice; the chain itself is a single unsigned association, so there is no route. The title's end points (abnormal sleep behavior, neuronal excitability) are not in the chain; the chain ends at RLS.

h3.note: sign read from the title 'PTPRD synaptic adhesion defects disrupt ...' and the mechanism 'PTPRD variants may disrupt synaptic adhesion and signaling' as loss of PTPRD function causing the disease; the falsification tests PTPRD knockout. The chain is a single unsigned association, so there is no route. The mechanism and falsification (not the title) name the variant rs34602324-G, which the chain does not.

findings.detail: The run cites nothing: every chain step has empty evidence, every hypothesis has empty supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence, and sources.json is empty, so no claim in the run can be checked against a text.

The question's budget sets min_evidence_per_hypothesis 2 and min_sources_per_hypothesis 2, yet all three hypotheses have zero evidence and zero sources, and the run neither abstained (abstention is null) nor flagged the shortfall.
Confidence 'high' with support 'speculative' and no evidence of any kind attached.
Confidence 'high' with support 'speculative' and no evidence of any kind attached.
Confidence 'medium' with support 'speculative' and no evidence of any kind attached.

The mechanisms quote GWAS rows (rs113851554-T p=1e-1371 beta=0.669; rs10947738-A p=1e-688 beta=0.282; rs34602324-G p=5e-162 beta=0.121), mouse phenotypes (abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle; abnormal sleep, mEPSCs, Purkinje cell morphology) and PTPRD partners (IL1RAP/IL1RAPL1, SLITRK2) as if read from records, but no accession is attached, so none of it can be checked.

The title claims MEIS1 transcriptional dysregulation causes circadian and motor control defects in RLS, but the chain is one unsigned association MEIS1 - RLS; no transcriptional program, neural circuit, circadian or motor node appears.

The title claims BTBD9 synaptic dysfunction leads to abnormal sleep behavior and neuronal excitability, but the chain is one unsigned association BTBD9 - RLS; synapse, excitability and sleep nodes are absent.

The title claims PTPRD synaptic adhesion defects disrupt sensory-motor circuits, but the chain is one unsigned association PTPRD - RLS; synaptic adhesion, partner binding and circuit nodes are absent.
Titles say 'causes' (h1), 'leads to' (h2) and 'disrupt' (h3), but each chain asserts only associated_with with unknown polarity, so no hypothesis states a causal step it could be tested on.

Each mechanism names a risk allele with a positive beta, but the chain drops the variant and sets polarity 'unknown', so the one directional fact the run states never reaches a step and no arm can compose.
The claim BTBD9 →− risk of RLS has no route: its only step is an unsigned association with no evidence.
The claim PTPRD →− risk of RLS has no route: its only step is an unsigned association with no evidence.
The gene subjects MEIS1, BTBD9 and PTPRD carry an empty curie and empty grounding_evidence; only the disease object is grounded (MONDO:0005391).
h1's falsification tests only whether rs113851554 associates with RLS (p<5e-8, OR>1.2), which would not test the claimed transcriptional, circadian or motor mechanism.
Half the question's genes (ACO1, GLIPR1, GABARAPL2) are listed as unexplained with no reason given and no abstention.

The guide's loss-of-function list (loss of, reduced, impaired, deficiency) does not say whether 'X dysfunction' (h2) or 'X defects' (h3) count, while 'dysregulates' (h1) is ruled undirected; I read the first two as loss of function (neg) and left h1 without a claim, which makes the three titles' signs a curator judgment.

A hypothesis-level causal claim with no direction ('MEIS1 dysregulation causes RLS') has no claim form, since claim signs must be pos or neg, so h1 leaves no claim row at all rather than an unsigned claim that is reported as untestable.

An unsigned gene-disease association never composes, so a run whose chains are all unsigned associations yields zero arms; the report shows 'no route' for h2 and h3 whether the cause is missing evidence or a missing sign, and these are different failures.

The run had nothing it could cite: in the store, all 8 specialist bundles (gwascatalog, uniprot, alliance, europepmc, string, reactome, hpa, opentargets) have items [] although 64 fetches returned artifacts (the only one of the 23 restless-legs study runs with an empty ledger), two delegations failed on output retries, the mechanisms copy their figures from the bundle summaries instead, and the run's own validation still accepted all three hypotheses with problems [].
